The Garden

Up close, and very personal.

ArtFlies Butterfly Garden is a living butterfly house tucked into the highlands of Valencia, a short climb west of Dumaguete City. Inside the screened conservatory, butterflies fly loose — feeding at nectar and fruit stations, resting on leaves, and often choosing a visitor as their next perch.

It was built as a place to interact with live butterflies up close and very personal — an educational tour for students, a field trip for a class, or an easy family morning out. There is an art corner where you can paint with the artist-owner, a playground for the children, and a nursery of potted plants and fresh harvest to take home.

Twenty to twenty-four days

Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, wings.

The whole journey happens right in front of you. Come back a few weeks after your first visit and the garden looks completely different.

  1. 01

    Egg

    A female lays a single egg on the host leaf — tiny, round, and usually hidden underneath.

  2. 02

    Caterpillar

    The larva hatches and eats almost constantly, moulting as it grows through five stages.

  3. 03

    Chrysalis

    It settles, hangs, and forms a pupa — the quiet stage where the whole body is rebuilt.

  4. 04

    Butterfly

    It ecloses with wet, folded wings, pumps them full, dries off, and takes its first flight.

The Residents

Meet the wings.

A few of the butterflies and moths you are most likely to meet inside the house — and the ones that headline our releases.

Release favourite

Lime Butterfly

Papilio demoleus

Black-and-cream swallowtail scattered with yellow spots and a fine red-orange rim. Tailless, restless, and everywhere in the garden.

Fast flyer

Tailed Jay

Graphium agamemnon

Velvet black dusted with emerald-green spots, with long trailing tails — a fast, restless flyer that never seems to sit still.

Blue Moon

Great Eggfly

Hypolimnas bolina

We call it the Blue Moon. Males are velvety black with glowing blue-violet ovals; females come in strikingly different forms.

Our release star

African Monarch

Danaus chrysippus

Also known as the Plain Tiger. Bright orange, black-tipped and unbothered — it floats slowly, which makes it perfect for a ceremony release.

Master of mimicry

Common Mormon

Papilio polytes

A widespread black swallowtail with a clean white band on the hindwing. The females are famous for mimicking other, unpalatable species.

Philippine swallowtail

Scarlet Mormon

Papilio rumanzovia

A large Philippine swallowtail washed in scarlet and rose across the hindwings — one of the most dramatic residents of the house.

Slow drifter

Grey Glassy Tiger

Ideopsis juventa

Translucent grey-brown wings crossed by dark veins and tiger banding. It drifts through the house slowly, almost hovering.

A giant

Golden Birdwing

Troides rhadamantus

One of the Philippines' largest butterflies: jet-black forewings held over hindwings that glow gold in the light.

A moth!

Philippine Atlas Moth

Attacus lorquinii

Not a butterfly but a giant silk moth — one of the largest in the world, with snake-shaped wingtips. Visitors know it as Mariposa.

What you can do here

More than a walk-through.

The Butterfly House

Wander the screened conservatory while butterflies land on you. Nectar and fruit stations keep them close, so you never have to chase a shot.

Educational Tours

A guided, curriculum-friendly tour for students, field trips and families — eggs, caterpillars, chrysalides and adults, all in one room.

Butterfly Releases

We provide live butterflies for weddings, birthdays and other events — a handful of wings released together at the exact moment that matters.

Ask about a release →

Art Sessions

A painting corner with the artist-owner Glory Abueva-Tobias. Paint what you saw in the house — a wing, a leaf, an entire metamorphosis.

Playground & Picnic

A play area for children to burn off energy after the tour, with plenty of shade for parents, teachers and birthday parties.

Plants & Harvest

Take a piece of the garden home — potted plants from the nursery and fresh, organic longkong lanzones when they are in season.
